story: At 7:17 on a cool, partly cloudy Monday evening in Sumter Oaks, Rosa is welcoming Donna and Hal into her house, where her warm curiosity about the visit shows in her teasing. Donna is in good spirits as she offers to help carry things to the table and explains that Gary has stepped home for a minute and will be along shortly. Hal arrives apologizing for being late, a little ashamed of losing track of the afternoon, and he offers to carry whatever needs moving. Meanwhile, Gary is back at his own house at the workbench, content and bench-testing the light strings and speaker wiring indoors, leaving the golf cart untouched until it's approved.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Bench-test the light strings and speaker wiring indoors, keeping the cart untouched until approval

gary.thought_process: I'm home at last after a long day: pickleball with Donna, then dinner at Rosa's. I told myself I'd stop running the cart wiring until Architectural Review signs off, and I filed the form back around tick 35, so the honest move is to keep the visible mods off the street until I hear back. But there's no law against tinkering inside my own house. The workbench is right here, and I can bench-test the lights and sound system without touching the cart or making a sound that carries. It's evening, so L-03 quiet hours aren't an issue yet, but I'll keep the speaker low anyway. It keeps my hands busy and gets the parade rig ready to bolt on the moment approval comes through.

parameters.content: Bench-test the light strings and speaker wiring indoors, keeping the cart untouched until approval

donna.thought_process: I'm at Rosa's with Hal and Rosa, and it's just past seven, so the six o'clock dinner is clearly underway or about to be. Gary just headed to his own house, which worries me a bit since he's meant to be here. Rather than fuss, I'll greet Rosa, thank her for hosting, and mention Gary will be along. It keeps me at the center of the table and sets up the pickleball ladder talk once everyone's settled.

parameters.content: Rosa, thank you for having us all! Gary's just run home for a minute but he'll be right along. Can I help you carry anything to the table?

hal.thought_process: I'm finally at Rosa's, and it's past seven, so I'm late for the six o'clock dinner. Memory says I owe her a real apology and should help carry things. Donna's here too, but the flamingo complaint can wait; I've been keeping too much of a ledger lately. Rosa first, plain and sincere, then offer to help.

parameters.content: Rosa, I'm late and I'm sorry. Lost track of the afternoon, and that's no excuse for a man who ran supply on a schedule for thirty years. Put me to work, I'll carry whatever needs carrying.

rosa.thought_process: Donna and Hal both just walked into my house at 7:17 PM Monday. The dinner is Saturday at six, so this is a surprise visit, and I haven't heard why they came. I've already invited both of them, so I shouldn't repeat the invitation. A warm, practical welcome and a plain question about what brought them is the natural move. If Hal came to talk about his absences, I'd rather hear it directly. It also gets two of my three neighbors in the same room, which is a small win for the table I'm trying to build.

parameters.content: Well, look who walked in at the same time! Come in, both of you. What's the occasion, Donna, did you two come to taste-test Saturday's menu early?

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
